text: Let a, b $\in$ R be such that the equation $ax^{2}-2bx+15=0$ has a repeated root $α$. If $α$ and $β$ are the roots of the equation $x^{2}-2bx+21=0$, then $α^{2}+β^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $ax^{2}-2bx+15=0$ has the repeated root $α$, its discriminant is zero:

$4b^{2}-60a=0\Rightarrow b^{2}=15a$

The repeated root is half the sum of roots:

$α=\dfrac{b}{a}=\dfrac{15b}{b^{2}}=\dfrac{15}{b}$

Since $α$ is also a root of $x^{2}-2bx+21=0$:

$\dfrac{225}{b^{2}}-2b\cdot \dfrac{15}{b}+21=0\Rightarrow \dfrac{225}{b^{2}}=9\Rightarrow b^{2}=25$

For $x^{2}-2bx+21=0$, $α+β=2b$ and $αβ=21$, so

$α^{2}+β^{2}=(α+β)^{2}-2αβ=4b^{2}-42=100-42=58$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: Let $z_{1}$ and $z_{2}$ be two complex numbers such that $z–_{1}=iz–_{2}$ and $\arg \left (\frac{z_{1}}{z–_{2}}\right )=π$. Then :

$\Rightarrow \arg (z_{1})=-\frac{π}{2}+\arg (z_{2})$ ..... (i)

Also $\arg (z_{1})-\arg (z–_{2})=π$

$\Rightarrow \arg (z_{1})+\arg (z_{2})=π$ ..... (ii)

From (i) and (ii), we get

$\arg (z_{1})=\frac{π}{4}$ and $\arg (z_{2})=\frac{3π}{4}$

text: If $b_{n}=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{\cos ^{2}nx}{\sin x}dx,n\in N$, then
options: $b_{3}-b_{2},b_{4}-b_{3},b_{5}-b_{4}$ are in A.P. with common difference $-$2
$\frac{1}{b_{3}-b_{2}},\frac{1}{b_{4}-b_{3}},\frac{1}{b_{5}-b_{4}}$ are in an A.P. with common difference 2
$\frac{1}{b_{3}-b_{2}},\frac{1}{b_{4}-b_{3}},\frac{1}{b_{5}-b_{4}}$ are in an A.P. with common difference $-$2
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$b_{n}-b_{n-1}=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{\cos ^{2}nx-\cos ^{2}(n-1)x}{\sin x}dx$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{-\sin (2n-1)x.\sin x}{\sin x}dx$

$=\frac{\cos (2n-1)x}{2n-1}\left |_{0}^{π/2}=-\frac{1}{2n-1} \right.$

So, $b_{3}-b_{2}$, $b_{4}-b_{3}$, $b_{5}-b_{4}$ are in H.P.

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{b_{3}-b_{2}},\frac{1}{b_{4}-b_{3}},\frac{1}{b_{5}-b_{4}}$ are in A.P. with common difference $-$2.

text:
If $y=y(x)$ is the solution of the differential equation 

$2x^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}-2xy+3y^{2}=0$ such that $y(e)=\frac{e}{3}$, then y(1) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$2x^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}-2xy+3y^{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow 2x(xdy-ydx)+3y^{3}dx=0$

$\Rightarrow 2\left (\frac{xdy-ydx}{y^{2}}\right )+3\frac{dx}{x}=0$

$\Rightarrow -\frac{2x}{y}+3\ln x=C$

$\because$ $y(e)=\frac{e}{3}\Rightarrow -6+3=C\Rightarrow C=-3$

Now, at $x=1$, $-\frac{2}{y}+0=-3$

$y=\frac{2}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: The value of 2sin (12${}^{\circ }$) $-$ sin (72${}^{\circ }$) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Write $2\sin 12^{\circ }-\sin 72^{\circ }=\sin 12^{\circ }-(\sin 72^{\circ }-\sin 12^{\circ })$ and use $\sin C-\sin D=2\cos \dfrac{C+D}{2}\sin \dfrac{C-D}{2}$:

$\sin 72^{\circ }-\sin 12^{\circ }=2\cos 42^{\circ }\sin 30^{\circ }=\cos 42^{\circ }=\sin 48^{\circ }$

So the value is

$\sin 12^{\circ }-\sin 48^{\circ }=2\cos 30^{\circ }\sin (-18^{\circ })=-2\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}\left (1-\sqrt{5}\right )}{4}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: The line y = x + 1 meets the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{4}+\frac{y^{2}}{2}=1$ at two points P and Q. If r is the radius of the circle with PQ as diameter then $(3r)^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let point (a, a + 1) as the point of intersection of line and ellipse.

So, $\frac{a^{2}}{4}+\frac{(a+1)^{2}}{2}=1\Rightarrow a^{2}+2(a^{2}+2a+1)=4$

$\Rightarrow 3a^{2}+4a-2=0$

If roots of this equation are $α$ and $β$.

So, $P(α,\qquad α+1)$ and $Q(β,\qquad β+1)$

$PQ=4r^{2}=(α-β)^{2}+(α-β)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 9r^{2}=\frac{9}{4}(2(α-β)^{2})$

$=\frac{9}{2}\left [(α+β)^{2}-4αβ\right ]$

$=\frac{9}{2}\left [\left (-\frac{4}{3}\right )^{2}+\frac{8}{3}\right ]$

$=\frac{1}{2}[16+24]=20$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: Let $A=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \end{array}\right )$ and $B=\left (\begin{array}{ll} -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 \end{array}\right )$. Then the number of elements in the set {(n, m) : n, m $\in$ {1, 2, .........., 10} and $nA^{n} + mB^{m} = I}$ is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \end{array}\right ]=A$

$\Rightarrow A^{K}=A,K\in I$

$B^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]=B$

So, $B^{K}=B,K\in I$

$nA^{n}+mB^{m}=nA+mB$

$=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2n & -2n \\ n & -n \end{array}\right ]+\left [\begin{array}{ll} -m & 2m \\ -m & 2m \end{array}\right ]$

$=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

So, $2n-m=1,-n+m=0,2m-n=1$

So, $(m,n)=(1,1)$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: Let $f(x)=\left [2x^{2}+1\right ]$ and $g(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} 2x-3, & x<0 \\ 2x+3, & x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$, where [t] is the greatest integer $\leq$ t. Then, in the open interval ($-$1, 1), the number of points where fog is discontinuous is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the number of points where $(f\circ g)(x)$ is discontinuous in the open interval $(-1,1)$, we first write the composite function explicitly.

The given functions are:

$f(x)=[2x^{2}+1]$

$g(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} 2x-3, & x<0 \\ 2x+3, & x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$

We can express $(f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x))$ as:

$(f\circ g)(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} [2(2x-3)^{2}+1], & x<0 \\ [2(2x+3)^{2}+1], & x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$

Let us analyze the continuity of $(f\circ g)(x)$ in three parts: for $x\in (-1,0)$, at $x=0$, and for $x\in (0,1)$.

Case 1: For $x\in (-1,0)$

Here, $(f\circ g)(x)=[2(2x-3)^{2}+1]$.

Let $u(x)=2(2x-3)^{2}+1$. 

As $x$ varies from $-1$ to $0$:

When $x\to -1$, $2x-3\to -5$, so $u(x)\to 2(-5)^{2}+1=51$.

When $x\to 0$, $2x-3\to -3$, so $u(x)\to 2(-3)^{2}+1=19$.

Since $u(x)$ is continuous and strictly decreasing on $(-1,0)$, its range is the open interval $(19,51)$.

The greatest integer function $[u(x)]$ is discontinuous at every point where $u(x)$ takes an integer value. The integers lying in the interval $(19,51)$ are:

$20,21,22,\ldots ,50$

Number of points of discontinuity in $(-1,0)$ is:

$50-20+1=31$

Case 2: At $x=0$

Value of the function:

$(f\circ g)(0)=[2(2(0)+3)^{2}+1]=[19]=19$

Left-hand limit:

As $x\to 0^{-}$, $(2x-3)\to -3^{-}$, which gives $(2x-3)^{2}\to 9^{+}$.

$u(x)=2(2x-3)^{2}+1\to 19^{+}$

Therefore, $\lim _{x\to 0^{-}}(f\circ g)(x)=19$.

Right-hand limit:

As $x\to 0^{+}$, $(2x+3)\to 3^{+}$, which gives $(2x+3)^{2}\to 9^{+}$.

$u(x)=2(2x+3)^{2}+1\to 19^{+}$

Therefore, $\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}(f\circ g)(x)=19$.

Since the left-hand limit, right-hand limit, and the value of the function at $x=0$ are all equal to $19$, $(f\circ g)(x)$ is continuous at $x=0$.

Case 3: For $x\in (0,1)$

Here, $(f\circ g)(x)=[2(2x+3)^{2}+1]$.

Let $v(x)=2(2x+3)^{2}+1$.

As $x$ varies from $0$ to $1$:

When $x\to 0$, $2x+3\to 3$, so $v(x)\to 2(3)^{2}+1=19$.

When $x\to 1$, $2x+3\to 5$, so $v(x)\to 2(5)^{2}+1=51$.

Since $v(x)$ is continuous and strictly increasing on $(0,1)$, its range is the open interval $(19,51)$.

The function $[v(x)]$ is discontinuous at every point where $v(x)$ takes an integer value in $(19,51)$, which are:

$20,21,22,\ldots ,50$

Number of points of discontinuity in $(0,1)$ is:

$50-20+1=31$

Adding the points of discontinuity from all parts:

$\text{Total points of discontinuity}=31+0+31=62$

text: The value of b > 3 for which $12\int\limits _{3}^{b}\frac{1}{(x^{2}-1)(x^{2}-4)}dx=\log _{e}\left (\frac{49}{40}\right )$, is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\int \frac{1}{(x^{2}-1)(x^{2}-4)}dx=\frac{1}{3}\int \left (\frac{1}{x^{2}-4}-\frac{1}{x^{2}-1}\right )dx$

$=\frac{1}{3}\left (\frac{1}{4}\ln \left |\frac{x-2}{x+2}\right |-\frac{1}{2}\ln \left |\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right |\right )+C$

$12I=\ln \left |\frac{x-2}{x+2}\right |+2\ln \left |\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right |+C$

$12\int\limits _{3}^{b}\frac{dx}{(x^{2}-4)(x^{2}-1)}$

$=\ln \left (\frac{b-2}{b+2}\right )-2\ln \left (\frac{b-1}{b+1}\right )-\left (\ln \left (\frac{1}{5}\right )-2\ln \left (\frac{1}{2}\right )\right )$

$=\ln \left (\left (\frac{b-2}{b+2}\right ).\frac{(b+1)^{2}}{(b-1)^{2}}\right )-\left (\ln \frac{4}{5}\right )$

So, $\frac{49}{40}=\frac{(b-2)}{(b+2)}\frac{(b+1)^{2}}{(b-1)^{2}}.\frac{5}{4}$

$\Rightarrow b=6$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: If the mean deviation about the mean of the numbers 1, 2, 3, .........., n, where n is odd, is $\frac{5(n+1)}{n}$, then n is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mean $=\frac{n\frac{(n+1)}{2}}{n}=\frac{n+1}{2}$

M.D. $=\frac{2\left (\frac{n-1}{2}+\frac{n-3}{2}+\frac{n-5}{2}+...0\right )}{n}=\frac{5(n+1)}{n}$

$\Rightarrow ((n-1)+(n-3)+(n-5)+...0)=5(n+1)$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{n+1}{4}\right ).(n-1)=5(n+1)$

So, $n=21$

text: Let $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+λ\widehat{k}$, $λ$ $\in$ R. If $\vec{a}$ is a vector such that $\vec{a}\times \vec{b}=13\hat{i}-\hat{j}-4\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{a}\quad .\vec{b}+21=0$, then $\left (\vec{b}-\vec{a}\right ).\left (\widehat{k}-\hat{j}\right )+\left (\vec{b}+\vec{a}\right ).\left (\hat{i}-\widehat{k}\right )$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $\vec{a}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}$

So, $\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ x & y & z \\ 1 & 1 & λ \end{array}\right |=\hat{i}(λy-z)+\hat{j}(z-λx)+\widehat{k}(x-y)$

$\Rightarrow λy-z=13,z-λx=-1,x-y=-4$

and $x+y+λz=-21$

$\Rightarrow$ Clearly, $λ=3$, $x=-2$, $y=2$ and $z=-7$

So, $\vec{b}-\vec{a}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+10\widehat{k}$

and $\vec{b}+\vec{a}=-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\widehat{k}$

$\Rightarrow \left (\vec{b}-\vec{a}\right ).\left (\widehat{k}-\hat{j}\right )+\left (\vec{b}+\vec{a}\right ).\left (\hat{i}-\widehat{k}\right )=11+3=14$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift
